decision: FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING — Frozen decision_rule triggers FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING on multiple independent clauses: (1) decompressed body-only discrimination 0.2911 < 0.3 threshold for JSON, HTML, and XML at all three sizes (conditions 1-3 fail); (2) decompressed hash variation all_same=false with unique_count=2 per state across all 9 conditions (condition 4 fails). Root cause is double-brotli encoding (scenario 4 of 5): single-pass client decompression strips outer brotli layer but leaves inner brotli-compressed data intact, producing a different hash (ddd198...) than the true decompressed body (6fb10...). The other 4 encoding scenarios (correct_br, missing_ce, incorrect_gzip, garbled_ce) all produce identical decompressed hashes deterministically. Discrimination without double_br is 0.4486 (above 0.3), confirming the failure is caused exclusively by the double-encoding scenario. Audit PASS confirms all recomputed metrics match producer. Claim ceiling does NOT advance from parent EXP-RUNTIME-35237982464: remains bounded to non-deterministic brotli quality variation on localhost only. NOT extended to encoding-layer double-encoding.

claim_updates.reason: Decompression-normalization sub-thread of C-MEAS-VALID: (a) survives single-layer encoding non-determinism (correct_br, missing_ce, incorrect_gzip, garbled_ce all produce identical decompressed hashes — verified in this experiment); (b) FAILS under double-brotli encoding with single-pass client decompression (discrimination 0.2911 < 0.3, determinism fails). Iterative decompression (decompress until failure or max depth) would restore the body (audit V6 verified manually: brotli decompress outer 74B -> inner 70B -> true body). The double-encoding failure mode is a client implementation issue, not a fundamental mechanism limitation. Product team must implement iterative decompression or reject double-encoded responses. Claim ceiling bounded to: localhost mock server + CDNEncodingProxy, synthetic padded JSON/HTML/XML, sizes 1KB-100KB, 4 auth states with 3-way error collapse (ceiling 0.5), brotli 1.2.0 single-pass fallback, no real CDN. Parent established discrimination 0.5 under quality-only variation stands. Real CDN infrastructure remains the critical untested blocker.

product_action: BLOCKED — Double-brotli encoding causes discrimination failure (0.2911 < 0.3) and determinism failure (2 unique hashes per state instead of 1). Real-CDN deployment for encoding corruption scenarios is blocked until the double-encoding failure mode is addressed via: (1) iterative decompression (decompress until failure or max depth), (2) Content-Encoding validation before decompression, or (3) rejection of double-encoded responses at the CDN/client layer. Single-layer encoding corruption (missing, incorrect label, garbled value) is safe — 4/5 scenarios produce identical decompressed hashes.
next_question: Does iterative decompression (decompress repeatedly until failure or a maximum depth of 3-5) restore decompressed body-only discrimination to >= 0.3 and decompressed hash determinism (all_same=true) under double-brotli and triple-brotli encoding on localhost — and does it maintain discrimination for the 4 single-layer encoding scenarios that already pass?
reason: The frozen decision rule FALSIFIES in this setting: discrimination 0.2911 < 0.3 (conditions 1-3) and determinism fails with 2 unique hashes per state (condition 4). The root cause is identified: single-pass client decompression on double-brotli encoding leaves inner compressed data, producing a different hash than the true body. Audit V6 confirms iterative decompression (brotli decompress twice) recovers the true body, so the mechanism is not fundamentally broken — the client implementation is insufficient. The 4 single-layer scenarios (correct_br, missing_ce, incorrect_gzip, garbled_ce) all pass identically, confirming the mechanism works when decompression succeeds fully. The next experiment should test iterative decompression as the fix, which is the smallest change that could restore the claim ceiling. Real CDN infrastructure remains important but should be deferred until the iterative-decompression fix is validated locally — testing CDN with a known-broken client implementation would confound CDN effects with client implementation effects.
